kind: Current-source original-response cache isolation cloud checks

reproduction.controlNote: Enable fixture then prime A; disable fixture then blocked cases; rotate actual producer Secret to B and re-enable fixture; seed B; in one bounded control step disable fixture and rotate Secret back to A; run negative Secret-A and positive literal-B control before B lifetime expires; restore resources. The unused rotated and checkB client branches were not executed.

adaptation.reason: Initial A entry expired before the first Secret update completed. No rotated-phase request was sent. Reverse direction B-to-A was verified with a still-valid B positive control rather than claiming an expired cache proved isolation.

limitations: One query family, one colo and small sample; not a complete cache-security matrix or reliability estimate.
Real Secret binding uses a public uncredentialed fixture URL, not an actual private credential; this tests reference/rotation semantics, not new credential redaction.
Different transport identity, ECS/DO variants, negative caching, signed DNSSEC rewrite combinations and persistent cross-colo behavior are not established here.
Producer code restored to original modules; current candidate is not left deployed.
Two run-specific original-response entries had at most 60-second lifetimes and were not globally purged; both lifetimes had elapsed before final cleanup checks.
No new CPU, profile, cold-isolate or ECH acceptance claim.
Fixture configured to reject DNS serving with HTTP 503; it was not shut down as a network endpoint. No claim of zero origin invocations.
